baseline.assignmentState: All seven package files matched the wave-two hashes. Scoped committed/staged/unstaged/untracked inspection found no pre-existing package edits.
baseline.finalAttribution: Only this review changed SKILL.md, references/token-validation.md, references/verification.md and skill.yaml. The other three references remain byte-identical to the snapshot. No shared or neighboring repository file was edited.

changes.finding: The skill covered multiple trusted issuers and issuer-specific authority vocabularies, but did not follow principal identity into the shared account/owner namespace. Stock JwtAuthenticationConverter 7.1.0 derives the principal name from sub, while JWT subjects may be unique only within their issuer. Two valid identities can collide if a downstream account/owner key drops the issuer.
changes.correction: Added a focused principal-identity section: preserve the validated issuer/subject pair or resolve it through an established trusted canonical account mapping; trace account lookups, owner references and authorization caches. Do not infer an account link from matching subject/email/display name or fall back from missing required identity to a shared account. Preserve adequate single-issuer or proven globally unique contracts and protect existing owners during a key/mapping transition.

changes.finding: The top-level authentication/permission workflow did not surface this identity handoff when adding an issuer.
changes.correction: Added a short reminder to preserve validated issuer/subject or canonical identity before ownership checks; no requirement to replace an adequate decoder/converter.

changes.finding: Existing hostile cases covered issuer rejection and wrong owners separately but not two accepted issuer namespaces with equal subject values.
changes.correction: Added same-sub/different-trusted-issuer mapping and owner controls, explicit trusted account links and missing required identity. Clarified that converter-only tests do not prove token validation or account/query isolation. Legitimate shared scopes or business permissions are not prohibited.

checks.details: Real NimbusJwtDecoder instances validated locally signed RSA tokens with configured issuer, audience, timestamps and explicit required-subject validator, then the real stock JwtAuthenticationConverter produced names and authorities. Two accepted issuer fixtures with equal sub produced equal names. An intentionally vulnerable synthetic owner comparison admitted the other issuer; a validated issuer/subject key retained the original owner and prevented the other caller's mutation. Explicit trusted canonical linkage remained possible. Wrong key, correctly signed wrong issuer and missing required subject were rejected. The required-subject rule is explicit probe policy, not a claim about generic defaults.
checks.boundary: Actual local decoder and converter; synthetic owner/account state and fixture issuer-selection map. Does not exercise HTTP filters, a Spring application context, Boot wiring, the production issuer resolver, a repository, cache, transactions, remote key retrieval, TLS or a deployed API.

walkthroughs: Only issuer A accepted: subject is within the established single-issuer namespace; issuer B must fail authentication before owner lookup. No identity-model rewrite follows from the existence of a foreign token.

Issuer B added with a separate subject namespace: both tokens can authenticate and equal principal names no longer establish equal accounts. Preserve issuer-aware identity at the existing account/owner boundary while retaining original owner data.
Established trusted canonical link: external issuer/subject pairs may intentionally resolve to one local account; different issuer values alone do not require denying an authorized link.

sources.support: Default JwtAuthenticatedPrincipal uses JwtClaimNames.SUB for its name; converter and principal customization remain explicit. Source evidence was corroborated with the cached 7.1.0 runtime.
sources.verification: Read tagged primary source and executed the actual class with two decoded tokens.

sources.support: A subject may be unique only within the issuer rather than globally. Subject and issuer comparisons therefore need the application's established identity contract.
sources.verification: Read subject claim scope and optional-claim context; no assertion that the generic JWT format universally requires sub.

sources.version: OpenID Connect Core 1.0 incorporating errata set 2; accessed 2026-10-16
sources.support: Adjacent identity evidence: OIDC's stable end-user identifier is issuer plus subject, while email/display claims have no equivalent uniqueness guarantee. Used to challenge automatic account-link assumptions, not to make ID tokens acceptable to this resource-server API.

limits: Only the local decoder/converter mechanisms were executed. The application-specific owner/account policy is a synthetic fixture, so no repository/query/transaction isolation or cache migration was proved.
The probe issuer allowlist is an explicit fixture map, not Spring's production authentication-manager resolver. Actual chain/resolver wiring remains an application-level test.
No HTTP service was started, no remote issuer was contacted by the Java probe, and no production credentials or real user identities were used. Test keys were generated in memory and not persisted.
Java source target is 17, execution runtime is 25.0.3; this does not certify a Boot application or execution on every supported JVM.
Original Boot, Java configuration and MockMvc examples were preserved; this review did not rerun them or broaden into an API deployment.
No independent behavioral actor, unseen holdout or measured skill-quality gain was produced.
No shared registry generation or repository-wide verification was run.

casePreparation.prerequisites: The actual resource-server issuer resolver/decoder contract is an explicit fixture premise. Subjects are unique within each issuer; there is no global-subject or account-link contract. Existing row 7 belongs to issuer A subject 42.

evaluatorCriteria.expected: Retain the adequate single-issuer identity mapping and require issuer B rejection at authentication. Do not force a new account model merely because another issuer has a token with equal sub.
evaluatorCriteria.observableFailure: Invent a reachable cross-issuer ownership bypass despite the stated allowlist, accept B based on matching name, or prescribe an unconditional identity migration.

evaluatorCriteria.expected: Correct the identity handoff using the validated pair or trusted canonical identity; preserve existing A owners, keep B authentication valid and deny B's unlinked caller access to A's row. Require a permitted control and unchanged denied state at the real application boundary.
evaluatorCriteria.observableFailure: Treat signatures/scopes as sufficient, keep getName as a global owner key without evidence, auto-link identities, trust unverified claims, strand A owners or remove B as a substitute for the required ownership correction.
